title: 摸鱼儿·更能消几番风雨
title_en: To the Tune of Mo Yu Er: How Many More Storms
author: 辛弃疾

text_note.zh: 本文用通行本（如邓广铭《稼轩词编年笺注》）。和语料库的文本有几处不同：通行本“惜春长怕花开早”，语料库作“长恨”；通行本“天涯芳草无归路”，语料库作“迷归路”；通行本“画檐蛛网”，语料库作“珠网”；通行本“休去倚危栏”，语料库作“危楼”。各本文字本来就有出入。另外，这首词原有一段小序，语料库没有收，内容见“背景”。
text_note.en: This page uses the common edition (for example, Deng Guangming's annotated edition of Xin Qiji). It differs from the corpus in a few places. The common text has cháng pà ("always afraid") where the corpus has cháng hèn ("always regret"). It has wú guī lù ("no road back") where the corpus has mí guī lù ("lost the road back"). It has zhū wǎng ("spider's web") where the corpus has a look-alike word meaning "pearl web". It has wēi lán ("high railing") where the corpus has wēi lóu ("tall tower"). Old editions really do differ here. The lyric also has a short preface that the corpus leaves out; see the background.

readings.zh: 这里读 gèng，意思是“再、还”，不读 gēng。
readings.en: Read gèng here, meaning "still, any more", not gēng.
In the name Sima Xiangru, this character is read xiàng.

readings.zh: “脉脉”读 mòmò，是含情不语、默默望着的样子；不读 mài。
readings.en: Read mòmò, meaning gazing silently with deep feeling; not mài.

readings.zh: “谁”现在口语多读 shéi，读诗时课本常标 shuí，两种都对。
readings.en: This character is often said shéi in speech today; in poems textbooks usually mark shuí. Both are accepted.

readings.zh: “不”在去声字“见”前面变调读 bú。
readings.en: Before a fourth-tone syllable like jiàn, bù changes to bú.

glosses.zh: 更能消：还能经得起。消，经受、禁得住。
glosses.en: gèng néng xiāo: how much more can it bear? Xiāo means to stand, to endure.
jǐ fān: a few more times.
cōng cōng: in a great hurry.
cháng pà: always afraid. Cháng here means "often, always".
luò hóng: fallen red petals, fallen flowers.
qiě zhù: stay a while, please don't go yet.
jiàn shuō dào: I hear people say.
tiān yá: the edge of the sky, the far ends of the earth.

glosses.zh: 芳草无归路：芳草长满天涯，把春天回去的路都遮没了。
glosses.en: fāng cǎo wú guī lù: sweet grass has covered the land to the sky's edge, so spring has no road back home.
suàn zhǐ yǒu: when you count it up, there is only.
yīn qín: eager and attentive, trying hard.
huà yán: painted eaves, the edge of a roof decorated with colors.
zhū wǎng: a spider's web.
jìn rì: all day long.

glosses.zh: 惹飞絮：粘住飘飞的柳絮。柳絮是柳树种子上白色的绒毛，像棉花一样飘。
glosses.en: rě fēi xù: catches the drifting willow fluff. Willow fluff is the white down on willow seeds that floats like cotton.

glosses.zh: 长门事：汉武帝的陈皇后失宠后，住在冷清的长门宫。相传她花重金请司马相如写了《长门赋》，想让汉武帝回心转意。
glosses.en: cháng mén shì: the story of Changmen Palace. Empress Chen of Emperor Wu of Han lost his favor and lived alone in the lonely Changmen Palace. Legend says she paid a fortune to Sima Xiangru to write a piece called the Changmen Rhapsody, hoping the emperor would come back to her.

glosses.zh: 准拟：本来料定、满心以为。
glosses.en: zhǔn nǐ: had fully expected.

glosses.zh: 佳期：美好的约会，这里指重新得到宠爱的日子。
glosses.en: jiā qī: a happy meeting; here, the day she would be loved again.

glosses.zh: 蛾眉：像蚕蛾触角一样细长弯弯的眉毛，代指美丽的女子。
glosses.en: é méi: eyebrows long and curved like a moth's feelers; it stands for a beautiful woman.
yǒu rén dù: someone was jealous of her.
qiān jīn: a thousand pieces of gold, a huge sum.
zòng: even if.

glosses.zh: 相如赋：司马相如写的赋。司马相如是汉代有名的文学家，赋是一种文体。
glosses.en: xiàng rú fù: a rhapsody by Sima Xiangru, a famous Han dynasty writer. A rhapsody (fù) is a kind of long, ornate writing.

glosses.zh: 脉脉：心里有很多话，却默默无言。
glosses.en: mò mò: full of feeling but silent.
shuí sù: to whom can I tell it?

glosses.zh: 君：你们，这里指那些嫉妒别人、得意的人。
glosses.en: jūn: you; here, those jealous people who are pleased with themselves.
mò wǔ: don't dance for joy.

glosses.zh: 玉环：杨玉环，唐玄宗的宠妃杨贵妃。
glosses.en: yù huán: Yang Yuhuan, Lady Yang, the favorite consort of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang.

glosses.zh: 飞燕：赵飞燕，汉成帝的皇后，很得宠。她和杨玉环最后都没有好结局。
glosses.en: fēi yàn: Zhao Feiyan, the much-loved empress of Emperor Cheng of Han. Both she and Yang Yuhuan came to bad ends.
jiē chén tǔ: have all turned to dust.

glosses.zh: 闲愁：说不出来、放不下的忧愁。
glosses.en: xián chóu: a vague sorrow you cannot name or put down.

glosses.zh: 危栏：高楼上的栏杆。危，高。
glosses.en: wēi lán: the railing of a tall tower. Wēi here means high.
xié yáng: the slanting sun, the sun about to set.

glosses.zh: 烟柳：笼罩在雾气里的柳树。
glosses.en: yān liǔ: willows wrapped in mist.

glosses.zh: 断肠处：让人伤心到极点的地方。
glosses.en: duàn cháng chù: a place that breaks your heart.

translation.zh: 还能再经得起几番风雨呢？
translation.en: How many more storms of wind and rain can it bear?

translation.zh: 春天又匆匆忙忙地要走了。
translation.en: Once again spring is hurrying away.

translation.zh: 我爱惜春天，总怕花开得太早，
translation.en: I love the spring, so I always fear the flowers open too soon,

translation.zh: 更何况现在已经落花满地。
translation.en: and now fallen petals lie everywhere.

translation.zh: 春天啊，请你先留一留！
translation.en: Spring, please stay a while!

translation.zh: 听说芳草已经长到天边，挡住了你回去的路。
translation.en: I hear sweet grass has grown to the sky's edge and blocked your road home.

translation.zh: 可春天不说话，真让人怨它。
translation.en: But spring says nothing, and I resent its silence.

translation.zh: 算起来，只有那殷勤的
translation.en: When I count it up, only one thing tries hard:

translation.zh: 画檐下的蜘蛛网，
translation.en: the spider's web under the painted eaves,

translation.zh: 整天粘住飘飞的柳絮，想把春天留住。
translation.en: catching the drifting willow fluff all day, as if to hold spring back.

translation.zh: 想起汉代长门宫的故事：
translation.en: Think of the story of Changmen Palace:

translation.zh: 陈皇后满心以为能重新得宠，好日子却一再落空。
translation.en: Empress Chen was sure the happy day would come, but it was missed again.

translation.zh: 只因为她美丽，曾经遭人嫉妒。
translation.en: Because she was beautiful, others were once jealous of her.

translation.zh: 就算花千金买来司马相如的好文章，
translation.en: Even if she bought a fine piece by Sima Xiangru with a thousand gold,

translation.zh: 满心的深情又能向谁诉说？
translation.en: to whom could she pour out the feelings in her heart?

translation.zh: 那些得意的人，你们别高兴得跳舞！
translation.en: You who are pleased with yourselves, don't dance!

translation.zh: 你们没看见吗？杨玉环、赵飞燕那样得宠的人，最后都化成了尘土。
translation.en: Don't you see? Even Yang Yuhuan and Zhao Feiyan, loved as they were, all turned to dust.

translation.zh: 说不出的闲愁最让人痛苦。
translation.en: A sorrow with no name hurts the most.

translation.zh: 不要去高楼上倚着栏杆远望，
translation.en: Do not go and lean on the railing of the tall tower,

translation.zh: 那落日正照着
translation.en: for the setting sun is shining just

translation.zh: 烟雾笼罩、让人伤心断肠的柳树。
translation.en: on the misty willows, a sight that breaks your heart.

background.zh: 词前有一段小序，说这首词写于淳熙六年（1179年）。那年辛弃疾从湖北调到湖南做管钱粮的官，同事王正之在小山亭摆酒为他送行，他就写了这首词。辛弃疾南归已经十几年，一心想带兵收复北方，朝廷却总把他调来调去，不给他重用。词里写春天留不住、美人被人嫉妒，其实是借这些说自己的心事。宋人罗大经的《鹤林玉露》记载，据说宋孝宗读了这首词，很不高兴。
background.en: A short preface says this lyric was written in 1179. That year Xin Qiji was moved from a post in Hubei to one in Hunan, managing taxes and grain. A colleague, Wang Zhengzhi, gave him a farewell feast at the Xiaoshan Pavilion, and Xin wrote this lyric there. Xin had come south more than ten years before. He longed to lead an army to win back the north, but the court kept moving him from post to post and never gave him real power. When the lyric talks of spring slipping away and a beauty envied by others, it is really talking about his own worries. A Song writer, Luo Dajing, recorded that Emperor Xiaozong was said to be displeased when he read it.

author_note.zh: 辛弃疾（1140—1207），号稼轩，南宋大词人。他生在被金国占领的北方，二十出头就带人起兵抗金，后来回到南宋。他一辈子想收复失地，却多次被冷落、罢官。他的词大多豪迈有力，这首却写得柔婉含蓄，把满腔的不平藏在惜春和美人的故事里。
author_note.en: Xin Qiji (1140–1207), also called Jiaxuan, was a great lyric poet of the Southern Song. He was born in the north, which was ruled by the Jin state. In his early twenties he led men to fight the Jin, then came south to the Song. All his life he wanted to win back the lost land, but he was often pushed aside or dismissed. Most of his lyrics are bold and strong. This one is soft and indirect: he hides his anger inside a story of spring and of a lonely beauty.

appreciation.zh: 上阕写春天要走了。词人先问：还经得起几番风雨？再求春天留一留，说芳草已经挡住了你回去的路。春天不理他，只有屋檐下的蜘蛛网，整天粘着柳絮，好像也想留住春天。这个小小的画面又可爱又心酸。下阕换成了陈皇后的故事：美人被人嫉妒，花千金买来好文章也没人听她诉说。接着词人对那些得意的人说：别高兴得太早，杨玉环、赵飞燕都成了尘土。最后不直接说愁，只说别去高楼远望，夕阳正照着烟雾里的柳树。愁就留在这片暮色里。整首词句句写春、写美人，其实句句写自己报国无门的苦闷。
appreciation.en: The first stanza is about spring leaving. The poet asks: how many more storms can it bear? Then he begs spring to stay, saying the grass has already blocked its road home. Spring pays no attention. Only the spider's web under the eaves catches willow fluff all day, as if it too wants to keep spring. This tiny picture is sweet and sad at once. The second stanza turns to the story of Empress Chen. A beauty is envied, and even a fine piece of writing bought with gold cannot carry her feelings to anyone. Then the poet tells the proud ones: don't be glad too soon; Yang Yuhuan and Zhao Feiyan are dust now. At the end he does not name his sorrow. He only says: don't climb the tower, for the setting sun is on the misty willows. The sorrow stays in that evening light. Every line seems to be about spring or a beauty, but really it is about his own pain at having no way to serve his country.
